integrity: An explicit algebraic proof gives the universal theorem. All numerical verification uses exact integer or Eisenstein-integer character arithmetic for five finite instances; no computation is represented as a universal certificate. No independent validation is claimed.
limitations: Only finite fields and dimensions a>=b>=2; no assertion for opposite rectangular range or nonfields. The exact formula gives individual multipliers but not a compressed eigenvalue-multiplicity table. Broader historical coverage remains a bounded-review priority risk.
title: Nonvanishing Fourier transforms of zero-composition matrix pairs in the stable rectangular range
